predictions.predict: 835 probed / 835 live / 0 missing — UNCHANGED. The file's sha256 CHANGES REGARDLESS, because `generated` is inside the bytes that are hashed.
predictions.why: the census's rows are the probes written inside tests/test-mechanics.js itself, not a scan of tests/probe_*.js — so the three probe files added by the narration close cannot add rows. The three engine fixes were narration-shaped (a -fail label, a redirect hoist, a terrain gate moved below Try). predictions.falsifier: any row moving WORKS -> MISSING is a regression this phase caused and must be attributed to one of the three fixes, not carried.

predictions.leg: the census's effect on the gate
predictions.why: under `--steering empirical` the whole-game artifact records `census_role: CREDITED ONLY — it measures coverage and does not select`, so a new census does not change WHICH games the whole-game leg plays. It does change the COVERAGE clause's denominator if any row moved, and it changes the steering digest that arms_comparable.js reads — which is why the runs either side of it are not a strict before/after even though the sample is expected to be identical.
predictions.risk: the coverage clause ('every used mechanic is measured by something') is the one that can move on a census change without any engine change at all.

predictions.why: the damage differential is unaffected by all three narration fixes and by the fixture swap; it was 0 of 6000 on 8ac9c4d888f1.

predictions.predict: GENUINELY UNKNOWN, and it is stated as unknown rather than guessed. The honest prior is that BOTH arms read board-material 0, because the tie die is shared and tests/test-resolution-order.js passes 26 arms; but no whole-game run has ever exercised these pins, and a corner arm is exactly where a tie-handling defect would hide.
predictions.why: a board that parts only at a corner is a tie-handling defect. A board that parts at BOTH corners is not a tie question at all — it is a defect the middle arm's pin happens to hide.
